page: Microsoft Azure DC4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, offering an even 4.0 GB of memory per core. The underlying processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and AVX.

Hardware accelerators are absent on the DC4as_v5, which features 0 GPUs, and the server does not include bundled local instance storage. Workloads requiring persistent disk storage rely on external remote storage attachments, such as Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking resources for external ingress.

Performance benchmark results show moderate single-thread compute capabilities balanced by comparatively modest multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests such as stress-ng (1990.57) and Geekbench (1224.0) fall within the middle 50% category, alongside baseline text processing (1569.0) and PassMark CPU encryption (2914.49). However, multi-core metrics place lower, with stress-ng multi-core (3963.09), Geekbench multi-core (2718.0), and the overall PassMark CPU score (4766.46) falling into the bottom 25% bracket. Similarly, Redis SET operations measured at 3.43 million operations per second, with the PassMark memory score reaching 1733.45.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the DC4as_v5 functions as a balanced, entry-tier general-purpose compute node. It is well-matched for microservices, lightweight web backends, CI/CD utility agents, and basic enterprise processing tasks that do not depend on dense parallel throughput, high-throughput in-memory caching, or local NVMe storage speeds.
